targets.approach: Leave the car beside the road above the Wilderness Permit Center, or use that center's lot. Begin just east of the turnoff to the permit center and Tuolumne Lodge and head north, uphill; a good trail begins a short way in but can be hard to spot the first time. The wall is east-facing and the first climbs come up after a short uphill walk, with the far end a little farther on. Alive at Leads climbs broken flakes to a single bolt on the slab above.
targets.name: Alive at Leads

targets.approach: The Entrance Boulder is just north of the south parking area at the Pinnacles: walk north along the side road a short way before you reach the lot. Its climbs face northwest. Not That Crack starts below and left of Short Stack and follows a left-slanting offwidth crack.
targets.name: Not That Crack

targets.approach: The Fins are a set of narrow pinnacles west of the Hungover Wall and Shirtsleeve Rock, both reached from Keller Peak Road. From the Shirtsleeve Rock area go up and over the north-facing rocks, then drop down to the visible pinnacles. The route is a thin, awkward left-facing corner crack in the inside corner right of the route Otto.
targets.name: The Fins

targets.approach: Drive Forest Road 2N86 to its end and walk south to the obvious boulder, across the road from Castle Grey Skull; the walk takes only a few minutes. The route is on the west face and laybacks a left-leaning, left-facing flake before face climbing past a bolt to the top.
targets.name: Forward into Battle

targets.approach: From the Pine Creek trailhead, an old road and then a trail lead to Lower Pine Lake. Go beyond Upper Pine Lake, but turn left before reaching Honeymoon Lake and cross Pine Creek Pass and drop into French Canyon. Where the first big waterfall tumbles down on the right from Merriam Peak's flanks, you reach the wall. The route climbs beside the waterfall, up a right-facing dihedral that turns into an arete.
targets.name: Meet Your Shower
targets.parent: Humphreys Basin, Pine Creek & Granite Park

targets.approach: The Gill Face is a short walk past the fence line at the south side of Holcomb Valley Pinnacles. John Gill is the single route on the left side of the face, on a south-facing block split by horizontal cracks, left of the route New Pygmy.
targets.name: John Gill

targets.approach: Take Gleason Ranch Road to the point beneath the rock and walk up from there; the other option is to come in from the east off Highway 178. The only route on the pyramid-shaped peak's north face begins in a fourth-class slot chimney.
targets.name: Bad Sneakers

targets.approach: The route is on a small band of south-facing cliffs at the junction of Gleason Ranch Road and Highway 178, just west of the Chimney Peak Road junction. It takes the longest, least broken face: from the boulders below, start on the right side of the face and climb to a bolt, then cross left on a dike to an arete.
targets.name: Joe's Route

targets.approach: Grouse Tor is the rounded summit east of the Grouse Ridge lookout; an easy walk from the parking area before the campground leads to the top, and a north-facing wall sits above Sanford Lake. Look for it at the rear of the big plateau high on the right side of the wall: after topping out Corn Silk, look right for a lone bleached pine in the talus field; the route is on the slab behind that tree. Another way to reach the plateau is to scramble down onto it from the face's west side.
targets.name: Wasted At IKEA

targets.approach: Walk from the parking spot to the first mini-crag, the Shooting Gallery, then wind down the canyon to the next crag, Gunslinger Rock, with its climbs on your left. Gym Climb is the face just left of the obvious crack on the west face.
targets.descent_text: There are no fixed anchors, so downclimb.
targets.name: Gym Climb
